     2	
     3	## Concept
     4	
     5	**Enterprise:** This digital twin represents part of JV Inkai, an in-situ uranium recovery operation in Kazakhstan. It focuses on three areas: MPP, Sat-1 and Sat-2. It also includes the area ion-exchange plants and the limit of MPP drying and packaging.
     6	
     7	**Users:** The main user is a wellfield production planner. This person plans when new blocks should receive acid and when they can start production. A production manager is a second user. They can use the twin to compare area production and possible curtailment. The model does not represent the internal logistics system of Kazatomprom.
     8	
     9	**Decision:** If sulphuric acid arrives later than planned, how do the acidification and start dates of new blocks change, and what happens to production under the plant limits? The twin compares a baseline with an adjustable delivery delay, using a fixed start order. It does not claim to find the best possible or a proven operating plan.
    10	
    11	**Why this choice:** I have always been interested in Kazakhstan's large mineral resources. I want to use data science to study a real problem in this area. Kazatomprom reported that changes in acid delivery timing in 2024 delayed the acidification schedule of new Inkai blocks. This happened even though acid requirements were fulfilled at 106% for the first nine months. Cameco later reported 7.8 million pounds of U₃O₈ production for 2024, compared with a target of 8.3 million pounds. This makes delivery timing a useful problem to study with a digital twin. I want the model to show its assumptions and compare scenarios instead of showing simulated results as real operating facts.
    12	
    13	**Real or fictional:** JV Inkai and its main operating details are real. This project is a representative simulation based on public sources. It is not a site-calibrated copy of Inkai. I will use public capacities and historical totals where available. Block group locations, individual block details, acid dose and duration, commissioning delays and production ramp-up are synthetic or assumed unless a source directly supports them. The map will be drawn for this project. It will not copy a published site figure.

    34	| `scenario` | Applied delay/day, baseline/delayed product/acid/WIP projections, assumptions and 27-case sensitivity grid. |

    37	
    38	Data path: model → MQTT `telemetry/org.minemind.inkai/<twin-name>` → platform MQTT source connection → Ditto `/features` → server-side Ditto REST reads → browser SVG/table/charts. `server.py` initializes twins with REST; **all runtime feature changes use MQTT**. All 18 twins must share one revision before a snapshot is served. There is no direct model-state fallback.
    39	
    40	Acid stock/commissioning is separate from uranium-bearing solution → area IX → aggregate recovered-U transfer → MPP drying queue. Satellite loaded-resin/eluate transport is omitted. Existing/sustaining-production acid supply is protected outside the commissioning boundary. No cross-area acid transfer is assumed.
    41	
    42	## Modules and What-if Scenarios
    43	
    44	| Scenario | What it does | How to see it on the Stand | How to undo |
    45	|---|---|---|---|
    46	| Acid-delivery timing and commissioning | Delay first deliveries by 0–42 days; second stays day 60. Changes stock, acidification/start dates, lifecycle, area flow, product and drying queue.     47

The sensitivity module runs the same accounting model over 27 cases: doses ×0.75/1/1.25, acidification 3/7/14 days and WIP targets 0/1/7 days. Every delayed case is compared with its own baseline. Results pass through MQTT and Ditto into the interface. The grid is illustrative, not evidence-based coefficient bounds, confidence intervals or a recommended policy. Runtime controls require no code changes. Applying delay recomputes a counterfactual from the same initial state. **View day**, **Advance 7 days**, and **Play days/Pause** expose the daily states.
    49	
    50	## What works and what does not
    51	
    52	Implemented: deterministic model, related twin definitions, MQTT publisher, Ditto-only gateway, spatial UI, adjustable delay, baseline comparison, stock/lifecycle/product display, bounded WIP and upstream pacing, the 27-case sensitivity module, complete reset and automated checks.
    53	
    54	**Verification:** The revised runtime passed a fresh full-stack Ubuntu WSL2 startup in 83.60 seconds with new credentials, isolated empty volumes and cached images/build layers. That run passed 29 unit tests (26 model tests and three mocked read-contract tests), 12 live application integration check groups and 23 full-platform smoke checks. Browser observations verified the spatial delay scenario and reset. Commands, source hashes, scope and logs are recorded in `team/inkai/EVIDENCE.md` and `evidence/fresh-stack-acceptance.json`. Cold image downloads, exact judge-KVM startup and real-world operational validation remain unverified.
    55	
    56	Not implemented: optimization, D1/D2 curtailment policies, outages, individual wells, chemistry/transport, company telemetry, probabilistic uncertainty forecasting or site calibration. The original Example Mine remains upstream reference only.
    57	
    58	## Data and Assumptions
    59	
    60	Detailed parameter inventory/equations: `team/inkai/PARAMETERS.md`; executable values: `team/inkai/config.json`.
    61	
    62	**Public facts:** Cameco's 2024 technical report, printed p.80, gives demonstrated IX capacities MPP 2.7, Sat-1 6.3, Sat-2 4.5 Mlb U3O8/year and MPP drying/packaging 8.3 Mlb/year; p.82 gives approximately 98% plant recovery. These are annual capacities, not measured instantaneous hydraulic limits. Kazatomprom's 3Q24 update supplies the qualitative acidification-timing mechanism and conversion 2.5998 lb U3O8/kg U. Cameco's annual filing, AIF p.67, supplies the contextual 7.8 Mlb 2024 actual and 8.3 Mlb target; neither is a fitting target.
    63	
    64	**Derived estimates:** annual Mlb U3O8 → daily kg elemental U: multiply by 1,000,000, divide by 2.5998 and 365. Uniform daily limits are a modelling approximation. `python3 -m team.inkai.report` reproduces the synthetic example. No chart digitization, 82% utilization or site acid-per-tonne ratio is used.
    65	
    66	**Synthetic:** group identities/positions, nominal rates and uranium inventories, commissioning-only tanks, delivery amounts/dates, planned starts and selected delay. No real block measurements or 2023 operating baseline are claimed.
    67	
    68	**Assumptions:** B1/B2 whole doses MPP 120/150 t, Sat-1 100/130 t, Sat-2 140/160 t; initial stocks 100/80/110 t. Each area receives 300 t on day 3 and 120 t on day 60; only the first arrival moves. Acidification is planned on days 5/18, starts only with the whole dose, takes 7 days, then ramps over 7 days. Constant head grade is 100 mg U/L; starting model uranium is 180 nominal-rate days per group. Proportional flow curtailment enforces area IX capacity and shared drying/WIP headroom. The assumed end-of-day WIP target is one drying-capacity day (8.75 t U), an operating rule rather than measured storage. Withheld potential extraction remains in the model uranium inventory. Nominal potential rates are unchanged; actual rates are capacity-paced. No toll processing is modelled. These block-level coefficients are not calibrated.
    69	
    70	**Simulated outputs:** every displayed state, stock, flow, start date, product total, difference and trajectory. Acid/uranium conservation establishes internal consistency, not operational validation. The 2% unrecovered stream preserves mass accounting; it is not destroyed uranium. A product difference is horizon-dependent, not a permanent resource loss.
    71	
    72	Sources:
    73	
    74	1. [Cameco 2024 Inkai technical report](https://www.cameco.com/sites/default/files/documents/Cameco-2024-Inkai-Technical%20Report.pdf), effective 30 September 2024, §§17.1
...[770 chars truncated]...
ate acid stocks, IX plants and shared drying/queue. Synthetic field footprints, symbolic well patterns, lifecycle colours, delayed-start outlines and live flow connections show consequences. Individual well symbols are not separate twins or measurements. Inspector, commissioning table, product/acid/WIP projections and the sensitivity grid all read platform state. Legend/disclosures distinguish public facts, synthetic inputs, assumptions, derived conversions and simulated outputs. Platform failure produces error/stale-state indication.
    83	
    84	## Limitations
    85	
    86	- Representative simulation, not site calibration or actual Inkai forecast/control.
    87	- Public capacities/mechanism are sourced; doses, durations, rates and schedules remain synthetic/assumed.
    88	- Commissioning-only acid boundary; no producing-group acid balance or acid-to-grade response.
    89	- Daily steps, fixed acidification/ramp and group order. Capacity limits extraction/processing, not administrative commissioning dates.
    90	- Annual-to-daily capacity approximation; constant recovery; no chemistry, transport, toll processing, energy or economics.
    91	- The illustrative sensitivity grid is implemented; operational validation is not. In the 28-day exercise, 3–6 groups start late across this grid while the product difference spans −61.66 to 0 t U. Different assumptions or bottlenecks mask product effects. No optimal schedule, probability interval or general production-loss estimate is claimed.
    92	- The one-day WIP rule assumes immediate daily coordination of extraction and processing. Actual storage, hydraulic limits, flow-ramp constraints and control delays are unknown.
    93	- Local WSL differs from the official KVM judge; startup coverage is documented in `team/inkai/EVIDENCE.md`.

    96	
    97	Root `presentation.pdf`: implemented scope, assumptions, supported evidence and instructions to observe/undo the scenario. No video.

     1	# MineMind: representative JV Inkai commissioning twin
     2	
     3	OpenEgiz Contest 2026 · Team 118 · solo participant `ahsan-h-shihab`.
     4	
     5	A source-informed **representative simulation** of how delayed sulphuric-acid deliveries can defer new wellfield commissioning. Nine synthetic groups in three areas connect acid stocks, lifecycle states, IX recovery and a bounded drying buffer. A 27-case assumption check exposes which conclusions depend on the selected coefficients. No site calibration, optimizer or actual operating forecast is claimed.
     6	
     7	## Install and start from this repository root
     8	
     9	Target: the [official judge environment](https://openegiz-contest.github.io/environment/), Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 with Docker Engine 29.1.3 and Compose 2.40.3. The judge already has Docker permissions and Python 3. Install `make`, which is absent from the judge base image:
    10	
    11	```bash
    12	sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y make
    13	make inkai-test
    14	make inkai
    15	make inkai-smoke
    16	```
    17	
    18	`make inkai` generates local credentials, starts the supplied OpenEgiz platform, builds the application, creates 18 Ditto twins, publishes their features through MQTT and confirms their ingestion. It waits for readiness and prints the UI address. No API keys, external datasets, cloud services or manual configuration are needed. The first run downloads the platform images and builds its pinned extended API; network time matters within the official 75-minute startup limit.
    19	
    20	The application adds only `paho-mqtt==2.1.0` to `python:3.12.12-slim`. All UI assets are included locally. Credentials stay in ignored `deploy/compose/.env`; never publish this file.
    21	
    22	## Open and demonstrate
    23	
    24	Open **http://localhost:8088/**, the submission's spatial interface. Grafana/OpenEgiz Twins remain at **http://localhost:3000/**; startup prints their generated credentials. The spatial UI needs no login because it is bound to localhost; Ditto credentials remain server-side.

    26	1. The application opens at **baseline day 30**, with operating flows visible. **Baseline · day 30** restores this view.
    27	2. Click **Delay 28 days · compare**. First arrivals move D3→D31. Six new groups wait for acid; the day-30 product becomes 188.16 t U versus 231.30 t U in the baseline.
    28	3. Click a representative field, tank or IX plant. Follow separate commissioning-acid stocks, wellfield states, solution-equivalent flow, IX recovery, bounded work in process (WIP), and dried product.
    29	4. Set **View day** to **38** and click **View day**: new groups start the assumed ramp after seven days of acidification. View **90** for the common-horizon comparison and equal delivered acid.

For a 28-day delay, 3–6 groups start late, but the day-90 product difference ranges from −61.66 to 0 t U. These are illustrative assumptions, not calibrated bounds.

Existing groups are labelled **ready** because no time has elapsed. The transport revision changes; physical state matches baseline day 0.

    33	Delay is 0–42 whole days. **Advance 7 days** and **Play days/Pause** traverse daily states. Applying a delay recomputes a counterfactual from the same initial conditions at the selected day. This is not a retroactive edit of a real operating event.
    34	
    35	The explicit operating policy paces extraction against area IX limits, shared drying capacity and an assumed one-day end-of-day WIP target. Capacity-withheld potential uranium stays underground; the WIP target is not a measured physical tank size.
    36	
    37	Purple stocks are **commissioning acid only**. Existing and sustaining-production acid supply is protected outside this model. Uranium-bearing solution goes to area IX; aggregate recovered-U transfer goes to MPP. Acid stock is separate from uranium/product inventory.
    38

It changes the running scenario; run it on a dedicated test instance when preserving a demonstration. `INKAI_NAMESPACE` and `INKAI_URL` must match the target; the namespace guard refuses a different Stand before sending controls. Actual results and clean-start coverage are in [`team/inkai/EVIDENCE.md`](team/inkai/EVIDENCE.md). Internal consistency is not operational validation.

    53	- `team/inkai/web/`: representative field footprints, process connections, controls, three projections, sensitivity table and inspector.
    54	- `team/inkai/compose.yml`: application overlay on the supplied platform.

Cold image downloads and exact judge-KVM startup remain unverified; see the evidence record.

    62	
    63	```bash

Port 8088 and upstream ports must be free. Platform failure produces a stale-state/error indication, never standalone model results.

Docker needs approximately 6 GiB available. The local WSL test machine is smaller than the judge's 16-GiB KVM environment; see the evidence record.

    73

No confidential/personal data, company PDFs, copied figures or third-party dataset is bundled. Research sources are references, not startup downloads.
